headline: The 20 km run held its efficiency gain, sitting almost entirely in Z1–Z2 at a lower comparable-effort HR.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days
confidence_attention: Limited data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
Your longest run of this block ran predominantly in the easy bands with only a token few minutes drifting into Z3, and the average sat comfortably in the lower HR range you've been holding across the block. That's the answer to a question worth asking: the efficiency signal that emerged during the volume ramp wasn't a recovery-week artefact — it held up when the distance climbed. Comparable-effort easy runs are genuinely running lower than the prior period across a solid sample, and this session extends that rather than breaking it.

The one thing this block hasn't tested is deliberate intensity. Time above easy remains minimal — the grey-zone fraction is tiny and Z2 minutes are still short of where a base block should sit. That's a load-distribution observation, not a fitness concern: the ramp itself was substantial, strength has been consistent, and the pilgrim crossing three weeks out favours durable time-on-feet over sharp sessions anyway. The DETRAINING strain flag reads that way largely because Polar's rolling window hasn't caught up to the recent volume, so I'd weigh it lightly against everything else the data shows.
watch_items: Whether the lower easy-run HR band survives the first genuinely hard or threshold effort, which this block hasn't yet included.
Whether loaded pack-carry running and sustained climbing enter the schedule with enough runway before the crossing.
Whether Polar's strain window catches up to actual load once a few more sessions accumulate, or the DETRAINING label persists implausibly.
Whether the short-night cluster settles, given how it may matter more as long-run frequency rises.

evidence_items.text: ▲ 4-week volume 181 km vs 94 km prior block (+94%)
▼ Easy-run HR averaging 142 bpm vs 151 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 10 vs 5 runs)
▼ Zone 2: 114 min vs 180-240 min/week target (63% of minimum); grey zone (Z3+Z4): 2.4%
